McLaren: McLaren’s latest tweak is a bigger front‑brake cooling duct, tailored to the demands of this circuit’s high‑speed corners. The extra airflow will keep the brakes from overheating, letting the drivers push harder for longer without losing grip. In short, the car will brake more confidently and stay quicker through the tight sections all weekend.
Mercedes F1 Team: The Mercedes front wing now has a reshaped middle section, moving from a three‑piece to a two‑piece layout, and the endplates and foot‑plate have been tweaked to match. This gives cleaner airflow over the car’s front, improving grip on the straights and in corners, so the team expects a stronger launch off the line and more consistent handling throughout the weekend.
Red Bull Racing: Red Bull has reshaped the front‑wing end plates and flaps to give the car a steadier, more planted feel through the corners, while an enlarged rear‑wheel exit duct improves cooling and reduces the chance of reliability problems. The tweaks should let the drivers push harder on the track without worrying about overheating or losing grip, giving them a solid edge for this weekend’s race.
